sampling_model.design: Choose \(d\in\mathcal D_L\); the focal design is \(d^\star=u\mathbf 1_p\).
sampling_model.treatment: Each unit receives mutually independent coordinates \(Z_{ai}\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(d_i)\), coded as \(X_{ai}=2Z_{ai}-1\).
sampling_model.overlap: Every dosage is interior; no claim is uniform as \(L\downarrow0\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The chosen \(\Sigma_k(d^\star)\) is known from the randomization, so no nuisance is estimated.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: For the additive model with \(k=1\), uniform limited-supply dosage is optimal up to a vanishing finite-sample factor.
Downward-closed hierarchical product designs satisfy an inverse-trace sum over products of marginal inverse-information excesses.
Matrix Chernoff bounds control both extreme eigenvalues of sums of independent bounded positive semidefinite matrices.
Random-design least-squares error separates covariance estimation, approximation, and response-noise contributions.
Volume sampling yields exact pseudoinverse expectations and an unbiased least-squares estimator under dependent subset sampling.

body.tldr: For independent product-Bernoulli assignment and the fixed complete Fourier basis through order \(k\), the population \(A\)-criterion is an explicit elementary-symmetric polynomial. Its unique shared-supply optimizer is the uniform dosage \(u=\min\{L/p,1/2\}\), with an exact criterion value and a global quadratic stability certificate whose coefficient is sharp when \(L\ge p/2\). Exact leverage and a rare-activation rank obstruction complement a two-sided threshold-OLS risk theorem. A fixed spectral threshold, the mean-zero whitened Gram, and a second-order inverse identity yield an explicit uniform \(O(n^{-1})\) relative-risk expansion at fixed dimension. This is oracle attainment at the population-optimal independent design, not finite-sample dosage minimaxity.

project_justification.gap: The modern PFED paper resolves limited supply analytically only for additive responses and reports numerical evidence for interaction models. Classical product-design theory gives the inverse-trace identity but not the shared expected-supply optimizer, its stability certificate, or the fixed-threshold second-order risk translation with fallback bias.
project_justification.niche: The fixed dosage-independent Fourier basis and downward closure permit an exact orthonormal triangular reduction, while the rank-one whitened rows expose both exact leverage and the second moment needed for a mean-cancelled inverse-Gram expansion.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the exact all-order criterion, proves uniform dosage with a global modulus whose coefficient is sharp when \(L\ge p/2\), and couples the design to exact leverage, rank-failure probability, the exact good-event/fallback risk decomposition, and a uniform \(O(n^{-1})\) fixed-threshold oracle-risk bound.

body.related_work: Shyamal, Zhang, and Uhler introduce the same product-Bernoulli factorial model and bounded-order Fourier regression, but their limited-supply closed form is additive-only. Schwabe and Wong provide the classical downward-closed product-design inverse-trace identity specialized here, so that identity is not presented as new. Tropp supplies the matrix-Chernoff engine for the empirical Gram event; the present second-order inverse calculation additionally uses the exact product-Fourier leverage bound and mean-zero whitened Gram to obtain the quantified relative-risk remainder. Hsu, Kakade, and Zhang motivate separating Gram conditioning from response noise in random-design regression. Dereziński and Warmuth obtain exact inverse-Gram expectations under volume sampling, a dependent design outside the admissible class here. Freise and Schwabe and Ravichandran and coauthors study restricted factorial regions or cell allocations under dependent randomization rather than independent coordinate dosage. Yao and coauthors are only an idealized high-multiplicity interaction-screen consumer: their application does not establish independent delivery or the homoskedastic Fourier regression assumed here.
body.technical_internal_limitation: At \(\beta=0\), spectral fallback can make finite-sample truncated risk smaller than the population \(A\)-risk. Thus the exact population optimizer is not asserted to minimize finite-sample risk over designs, and no minimax claim follows from the risk sandwich.
body.honest_scope: The note establishes the exact population identity and optimizer, a global stability modulus whose coefficient is sharp only when \(L\ge p/2\), exact leverage, the rank obstruction, the finite-sample risk sandwich, and a fixed-threshold uniform \(O(n^{-1})\) oracle-risk expansion at fixed \(p,k,L,B,\sigma_{\min},\sigma_{\max}\). Exact finite-sample minimax dosage remains open. The core excludes dependent or fixed-count assignment, growing dimension, heteroskedastic outcomes, adaptive rounds, model misspecification, and uniformity as supply vanishes. The Yao application is only an idealized consumer under independent delivery and the stated regression model.
